[Jeffrey M. Girard | Lecture {{< meta lecture >}}]{} ::: ![](../../img/proud_coder_357EDD.svg){.absolute bottom=30 right=0 width="400"} ::: ## Roadmap ::: {.columns .pv4} ::: {.column width="60%"} - Learn how to summarize whole datasets - Learn how to summarize data by distinct groups ::: ::: {.column .tc .pv4 width="40%"} {{< lif "../../icons/map.json" trigger=hover colors=secondary:#2a76dd class=rc >}} ::: ::: # Summarize ## Summarize {.smaller} ::: {.columns .pv4} ::: {.column width="60%"} - Although we store data about many observations... - ...we often want to [summarize across]{.b .blue} observations - This is like [folding]{.b .green} the tibble down to [one row]{.b .green} ::: {.fragment .mt1} - We have seen functions that summarize vectors - `length()`, `sum()`, `min()`, `max()` - `mean()`, `median()`, `sd()`, `var()` ::: ::: {.fragment .mt1} - `summarize()` lets us use them on tibbles - It works very similarly to `mutate()` - It always creates a tibble as output ::: ::: ::: {.column .tc .pv4 width="40%"} {{< lif "../../icons/fold.json" trigger=loop delay=3000 colors=secondary:#2a76dd class=rc >}} ::: ::: ## 1. Preparing the Data ::: {.fsmaller} First, let's create a small example dataset of sales to practice our summary functions. ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} library(tidyverse) sales <- tibble( customer = c(1, 2, 3, 1, 3), store = c("A", "A", "A", "B", "B"), items = c(25, 20, 16, 10, 5), spent = c(685, 590, 392, 185, 123) ) sales ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 5 × 4 customer store items spent 1 1 A 25 685 2 2 A 20 590 3 3 A 16 392 4 1 B 10 185 5 3 B 5 123 ``` ::: ::: ## 2. Basic Summarize ::: {.fsmaller} We can use `summarize()` to calculate the average items and spent across all observations in the dataset. ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} sales |> summarize( avg_items = mean(items), avg_spent = mean(spent) ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 1 × 2 avg_items avg_spent 1 15.2 395 ``` ::: ::: ## 3. The `summary()` Pitfall ::: {.fsmaller} **Warning:** Be careful not to accidentally use base R's `summary()` function when you mean to use `dplyr::summarize()`. The former will not return a tidy tibble. ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} sales |> summary( avg_items = mean(items), avg_spent = mean(spent) ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` customer store items spent Min. :1 Length:5 Min. : 5.0 Min. :123 1st Qu.:1 Class :character 1st Qu.:10.0 1st Qu.:185 Median :2 Mode :character Median :16.0 Median :392 Mean :2 Mean :15.2 Mean :395 3rd Qu.:3 3rd Qu.:20.0 3rd Qu.:590 Max. :3 Max. :25.0 Max. :685 ``` ::: ::: ## 4. Counting Functions ::: {.fsmaller} We can also use special functions like `n()` to count total rows, and `n_distinct()` to count unique values. ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} sales |> summarize( n_sales = n(), n_customers = n_distinct(customer), n_stores = n_distinct(store) ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 1 × 3 n_sales n_customers n_stores 1 5 3 2 ``` ::: ::: # Grouped Summarize ## Grouped Summarize {.smaller} ::: {.columns .pv4} ::: {.column width="60%"} - We can also summarize a tibble [by group]{.b .blue} - This is like [folding]{.b .green} the tibble multiple times - Specifically, we fold down to [one row per group]{.b .green} ::: {.fragment .mt1} - We just add the `.by` argument to `summarize()` - We can group by one or many variables - With many, we group by their combinations ::: ::: ::: {.column .tc .pv4 width="40%"} {{< lif "../../icons/origami.json" trigger=loop delay=3000 colors=secondary:#2a76dd class=rc >}} ::: ::: ## 1. Summarizing by One Group ::: {.fsmaller} Let's see how the sales perform on a per-store basis by adding the `.by` argument. ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} sales |> summarize( customers = n_distinct(customer), items_sold = sum(items), total_sales = sum(spent), avg_items = mean(items), avg_spent = mean(spent), .by = store ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 2 × 6 store customers items_sold total_sales avg_items avg_spent 1 A 3 61 1667 20.3 556. 2 B 2 15 308 7.5 154 ``` ::: ::: ## 2. Summarizing by Multiple Groups ::: {.fsmaller} If we pass multiple variables to `.by`, it summarizes every unique combination of those groups. ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} sales |> summarize( n_visits = n(), items_bought = sum(items), total_spent = sum(spent), .by = c(customer, store) ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 5 × 5 customer store n_visits items_bought total_spent 1 1 A 1 25 685 2 2 A 1 20 590 3 3 A 1 16 392 4 1 B 1 10 185 5 3 B 1 5 123 ``` ::: ::: ## 3. Real-World Data ::: {.fsmaller} Let's apply these concepts to a larger, more realistic dataset using `nycflights13`. ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} library(nycflights13) flights |> select(month, day, carrier, flight, dep_delay) |> head() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 6 × 5 month day carrier flight dep_delay 1 1 1 UA 1545 2 2 1 1 UA 1714 4 3 1 1 AA 1141 2 4 1 1 B6 725 -1 5 1 1 DL 461 -6 6 1 1 UA 1696 -4 ``` ::: ::: ## 4. Flight Delays by Carrier ::: {.fsmaller} We can find the carrier with the lowest average departure delays by grouping and sorting. Note that we need `na.rm = TRUE` to ignore missing values. ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} flights |> summarize( m_delay = mean(dep_delay, na.rm = TRUE), .by = carrier ) |> arrange(m_delay) |> head() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 6 × 2 carrier m_delay 1 US 3.78 2 HA 4.90 3 AS 5.80 4 AA 8.59 5 DL 9.26 6 MQ 10.6 ``` ::: ::: ## 5. Busiest Days of the Year ::: {.fsmaller} By grouping by both `month` and `day`, we get 365 rows instead of just 31 (which would happen if we only grouped by `day`). ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} flights |> summarize( n_flights = n(), .by = c(month, day) ) |> arrange(desc(n_flights)) |> head() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 6 × 3 month day n_flights 1 11 27 1014 2 7 11 1006 3 12 2 1004 4 7 8 1004 5 7 10 1004 6 7 18 1003 ``` ::: :::
